SSD-DC- HDC3 (Thermal Event, corrugate auger) On 3/7/2026, at approximately 2242 hrs, a burning odor was detected in the trash compactor / corrugate auger area. Operations and Safety personnel responded to assess the situation. Smoke was observed coming from the compactor system, and an attempt was made to suppress the fire using a portable fire extinguisher; however, the fire continued to produce smoke. Due to increasing smoke and visible fire conditions, the decision was made to activate the site fire alarm and initiate a full building evacuation. All associates evacuated in accordance with emergency procedures and reported to designated assembly areas where headcounts were conducted and all personnel were accounted for. The local Fire Department responded, extinguished the fire within the compactor system, and cleared the scene. Following fire suppression activities, a site Safety Specialist conducted air quality monitoring within the facility prior to resumption of normal operations.

initial_info_incident_description: Video footage shows that at 10:55:34 the 3rd regulator on the right side of the propane tank ruptured, visible flare up can be seen.  Guard shack officer is notified at 11:10 by a truck driver that there was an open flame up by the front entrance of the road.  Security notifies a manager at 11:30 pm.  Ops Manager and Security notify CBRE to check it out at 12:00 am  per security incident report.    Attempting to locate the source of the flame CBRE initially went to the hydrogen tank (located at the opposite side of the building) not seeing any flames they realized that it was the propane tank.  At 12:13 am CBRE informs security that there was a fire near the propane tank and to notify the authorities.  (11 was contacted at 12:13 am.  Police and fire department arrived on scene at 12:21 am.  Cleared the premises at 01:12 am.  Building evacuation commenced at 12:10 am, all clear issued by the fire department at 01:10 hrs.  Penn Valley Systems was contacted and arrived at the site at 3:27 am. The dispatched tech explained that there are 2 lines that feed the regulator tanks. The tanks transpose the liquid propane supply to gas. There is a main regulator line that has an emergency shut off button and a back up line that feeds the regulator tanks that is all manually shut off. The 3 regulator tanks have an electrical pilot lighting system.  Technician shut off all valves supplying the three regulator tanks, on both supply lines. After the tanks there are also two supply lines to the building. Technician drained and bled both supply lines to the building. Lastly the technician shut off the actual supply feed valve right at the building and verified no gas pressure. The tech will be contacting Hiltz propane systems to ensure that they will be coming out to determine cause
initial_info_fire_description: Undetermined at this time pending further investigation however it is believed that  a fitting came loose which allowed propane to seep through flowing down to the vent which acted as the gas source and in turn ignited due to the proximity of the vapor flame.

RME to obtain quote and explore possibility of replacing existing vaporizers with electric model (Owner: qumorgar, ECD 10/16/2024, 5.  Partner with security/LP to put a process in place to open fenced in Rally Point Area, (owner: hwwagone, ECD – 10/14/2024), 6.  Create webhook in manager slack whereby managers need to put a snip of their updated rally point app to show that they have updated their app (Owner: ttkania, ECD- 10/14/2024)

initial_info_incident_description: SSD-DC – HGA6 (Serious Incident Near Miss, Fire) SSD-DC – HGA6 (Serious Incident Near Miss, Fire)- On 6/11/2024 at 2:27 PM , WHS was notified of smoke coming from the cardboard auger. Shortly after responding to the incident the fire alarm was activated and the site was evacuated. Upon further investigation it was found that the auger was stuffed with carboard at 100% fullness.  As the auger began to spin after placing more cardboard in it, it caused friction between the compact carboard and the auger which caused it to heat up. The combination of the heat from the carboard and the outside temperature caused a fire to start in the container. After the investigation, it was found that all Waste Management containers flag at 75% fullness in which the company is notified to come on site and change the containers. In this case, Waste Management had not yet been on site to change the containers. It was also found that the cardboard conveyors from the UIS lane don't run automatically once it hits this threshold. However, in this case 10 minutes before the fire started an AA from ABM was standing holding the override button on the side of the auger which caused the machine to run even though it was 100% full.

initial_info_incident_description:
SSD-DC – HNE1 (Serious Incident Near Miss, Fire) SSD-DC – HNE1 (Serious Incident Near Miss, Fire)-On June 25, 2024, at approximately 09:54 AM EST, the site safety team was alerted to a fire involving the cardboard compactor auger at OB Dock 145. The fire alarm was promptly activated, and a site-wide evacuation was carried out to ensure the safety of all personnel.
Upon investigation, it was determined that the root cause of the fire was not related to the compactor container being at full capacity. At 9:15 AM, the compactor container was only at 20% capacity, holding approximately 3,200 lbs of material, whereas its full capacity is 16,000 lbs. Further investigation revealed that the previous container had been replaced with an empty one at approximately 6:00 AM. The delay in replacing the full container on time led to a significant backlog of cardboard shuttle containers.

Due to this delay, ABM associates had staged and piled up more than 35 cardboard shuttle containers, awaiting the emptying of the compactor container. Once the container was emptied at 6:00 AM, the associates began disposing of the accumulated cardboard into the compactor auger from 6:55 AM through 9:54 AM. Additional cardboard from HNE1 and LGA5 continued to be disposed of, exacerbating the situation.
The continuous disposal of a large volume of cardboard without allowing the compactor auger to cool down resulted in the equipment overheating. This overheating caused fire friction, igniting the cardboard and leading to the fire incident.

The root cause of the incident has been identified as fire friction due to the excessive use of the compactor auger for more than three hours without a cooling period. This was a direct consequence of the backlog created by the delayed replacement of the full compactor container.
initial_info_fire_description: There was a friction fire caused by the augers due to the overuse of the compactor auger without allowing it to cool down

initial_info_incident_description: On 3/14/24, around 2:05pm an associate's vehicle started on fire in the parking lot. CCTV footage shows the AA parking and walking away from the vehicle when it began to smoke and catch fire. The fire spread to several other vehicles that were parked nearby as well. The Fire department arrived on scene and put the fire out. The fire department is still on scene and awaiting an arson investigator. The sit conducted a shelter in place drill to get all AAs accounted for. No evacuation or shelter in place was implemented due to the fire department's advice to keep everyone safe inside. No EMS/Police dispatched. No injuries reported. No trouble ticket created. The WHS team is currently working on scheduling a vendor to attend the site for clean-up support. Two additional vehicles were impacted by the fire; all three vehicles will need to be towed for clean-up to occur. The vehicle owners are awaiting guidance from their insurance companies for tow / removal of the vehicles. Images have been sent to vendor, Clean Harbors, who are in contact with their local team to determine scheduling for clean-up. Local fire department (FD) left the site, and no root cause has been provided at this time. FD will return to the site on 03/15/2024 to collect footage and further analyze root cause. FD did use their hoses to stop the fire, and debris still remains on the ground. There are no drains in the immediate area of the event; however, WHS has informed Clean Harbors that they will need to check the storm drains as part of the clean-up. There is a chance of scattered storms in the area today and tomorrow. The exact location of the fire was at the bushes next to the smoker’s area. Fire department responded to the fire onsite at 23:15 and GSOC was notified of the incident. There were no injuries reported and the smoke did not affect the operation or personnel. Video footage of the incident is being review and root cause is pending further investigation.
